# Origin

## Strain-Counterstrain

Strain-Counterstrain was developed by Dr. Lawrence Jones


## Fascial Counterstrain

Dr. Brian Tuckey was 1 of 4 practitioners personally certified by Dr. Jones to teach Counterstrain before Dr. Jones' death.

# Fascial Counterstrain

# Causes of Fascial Dysfunction

@tuckeyFCSF1Foundations2024
- Trauma (PS or CNS structures)
- Surgery
- Postural strain
- Overuse/repetitive strain
- Structural strain (Leg length discrepancy, malocclusion, pronation etc.)
- Inflammatory diseases (lyme, Chron's etc. )
- Fibromyalgia/food sensitivities

# Precuations and Contraindications

@tuckeyFCSF1Foundations2024

FCS Precautions

- Acute infection (prior to antibiotic prescription)
- Increased pain/symptoms or apprehension reported by the patient during application of the technique
- Implanted devices (stents, pacemakers, IUD's etc.)
- Lack of experience with the associated condition / pathology
- Increased pain or apprehension experienced during a release

FCS Contraindications

- Aneurisms including pulsing abdominal masses (possible aortic aneurysm)
- Deep vein thrombosis (vascular knee techniques) - unless declared stable
- Any other situation in which manipulation or soft tissue work may be contra-indicated
   - unhealed fractures
   - unhealed incisions
   - immobilized structures

# Conclusions

## Cons

- Multiple failure points

## If true

- Provides a system for assessing multiple regions and systems
- Expands treatments from muscle, bones, and joints to include visceral, arterial, venous, lymphatic, and nervous tissues



# Main Conclusions

## Fascia

Thinking about fascia as a passive tissue is an oversimplification.

There are articles against manual therapy for fascia claiming that it is impossible to significantly change fascia through manual therapy

We should be considering fascia within the context of inflammation in the environment

## Multi-system consideration

- Regardless of treatment philosophy/school, considering venous, nervous, arterial, and visceral structures along with musculoskeletal structures will only give you a clearer picture of your patient
